scope: Airport and airport-authority custom-footprint overlap cases already accepted into production

cases.recommended_build_method: Build a two-county airport property polygon by joining Tarrant and Dallas cadastral geometry to their appraisal-roll ownership tables, selecting airport-board-owned airport-campus parcels on both sides of the county line, dissolving them into one multipart polygon, and validating parcel inclusion against the official DFW tract map and land-use map.
recommended_build_path: Tarrant County side: use https://www.tad.org/content/gis-data/2025ESRI_Parcels.zip together with https://www.tad.org/content/data-download/PropertyData_2025(Certified).ZIP to recover owner-linked parcel polygons.

Dallas County side: use https://www.dallascad.org/ViewPDFs.aspx?type=3&id=%5C%5CDCAD.ORG%5CWEB%5CWEBDATA%5CWEBFORMS%5CGIS%20PRODUCTS%5CPARCEL_GEOM.zip and follow https://www.dallascad.org/PARCEL_GEOM.pdf to join geometry back to appraisal attributes.

QA and cleanup: compare the dissolved parcel bundle to the official DFW tract map https://dfwairport-prd-dfw-vip.dfwairport.com/cs/groups/webcontent/documents/webasset/p2_139343.pdf and land-use map https://dfwairport-prd-dfw-vip.dfwairport.com/cs/groups/webcontent/documents/webasset/p3_102231.pdf before computing block-group weight shares.

sources.title: Tarrant Appraisal District certified property roll

source_hierarchy.reason: Official county cadastral geometry and official airport maps are sufficient; no public fallback is needed.

validation_notes: I did not find a public single-file official DFW property-boundary polygon. The parcel-assembly path is still production-usable because both counties publish official parcel geometry and DFW publishes tract and land-use maps for QA.
Treat the tract map as the arbitration source if owner-name matching captures airport-related but non-campus holdings.

cases.agency: BWI / Maryland Aviation Administration airport case
cases.recommended_build_method: Build the footprint from the official Anne Arundel County parcel layer by selecting contiguous BWI campus parcels owned by Maryland Aviation Administration or equivalent State of Maryland aviation-owner variants, dissolve them, and use the official BWI environmental-review figures to confirm the airport property edge and remove any off-campus owner matches.
recommended_build_path: Primary geometry: https://gis.aacounty.org/arcgis/rest/services/OpenData/Planning_OpenData/MapServer/34 queried through owner fields such as ASST_FIRST_OWNER and ASST_SECND_OWNER.

QA and cleanup: validate the parcel union against the official 2020 Final EA/FONSI-ROD https://marylandaviation.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/111220_Final%20EA%20and%20Section%204f%20Determination%20and%20Finding%20of%20No%20Significant%20Impact%20%20Record%20of%20Decision.pdf and Appendix H https://marylandaviation.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/111220_Appendix%20H%20-%20Biological.pdf.
Final geometry: dissolved airport property polygon ready for block-group intersection.

cases.recommended_build_method: Build a near-exact airport-campus polygon from the official airport ArcGIS organization by unioning the ATL_Airfield operational polygons with official ATL surface-transportation and building polygons, then use the official Clayton County parcel layer to validate airport ownership and fill landside airport parcels. This is production-usable even though I did not find a single public legal property-boundary polygon.
recommended_build_path: Operational footprint: https://services5.arcgis.com/62o2qANhRqripAuB/arcgis/rest/services/ATL_Airfield/FeatureServer with emphasis on AirOperationsArea Apron Infield MovementArea RunwaySafetyAreaBoundary and RW_TW_SafetyZoneMerge.

Ownership QA: https://gis.claytoncountyga.gov/server/rest/services/TaxAssessor/Parcels/MapServer/0 filtered with airport parcel signatures such as OWNERNME = CITY OF ATLANTA, SITEADDRES = ATLANTA INTL AIRPORT, APPRAREA = 333, and airport land-use categories.
Final geometry: dissolve the unioned airport-operated polygons and parcel-backed landside polygons into one multipart footprint.

cases.agency: MWAA Police (Reagan National + Dulles + Dulles roadway facilities)
cases.recommended_build_method: Build a multi-facility authority footprint by using bounded Reagan and Dulles airport-campus proxies from the live Virginia block-group lattice, validating those proxies against the official DCA EA and Dulles master-plan / ALP materials, extracting the Dulles roadway facilities from official VDOT Route 267 GIS, buffering those routes conservatively, and unioning the airport and roadway geometries into one multipart MWAA police footprint.
recommended_build_path: Reagan airport component: use special Virginia block group 510139802001 as the bounded public Reagan campus proxy after validating its shape and acreage against https://www.mwaa.com/sites/mwaa.com/files/2024-03/dca_roadway_ea_v1_final_ea_20231213_signed.pdf and https://www.mwaa.com/sites/mwaa.com/files/2024-03/dca_roadway_ea_v2_final_ea_appendices_20240111.pdf.

Dulles airport component: use special Virginia block groups 510599802001 and 511079801001 as the bounded public Dulles campus proxy after validating their combined acreage and map fit against https://www.flydulles.com/airport-overview and the Dulles master-plan / ALP materials.

Roadway facilities: extract Route 267 segments from https://services.arcgis.com/p5v98VHDX9Atv3l7/arcgis/rest/services/VDOT_Routes/FeatureServer inside the Dulles corridor and buffer them conservatively to represent the MWAA-policed Dulles Access Road and Dulles Toll Road facilities.
Final geometry: multipart union of the Reagan proxy BG, the two Dulles proxy BGs, and the buffered Dulles roadway corridor, then intersect that union with 2020 Virginia TIGER block groups.

source_hierarchy.note: This is the primary buildable roadway-geometry source for the Dulles facilities component; the airport components close through official-doc QA against bounded airport-campus proxies.

sources.title: IAD Airport Layout Plan drawing set

source_hierarchy.reason: Official GIS and official airport-authority plan documents are sufficient for a production build.

validation_notes: The roadway piece is near-exact rather than exact because the public VDOT source is a centerline layer, not a surveyed right-of-way polygon; a conservative buffer is therefore preferable to pretending there is a legal corridor polygon.

The airport components are not hand-digitized polygons; they are bounded special airport block-group proxies whose acreage closely matches the official Reagan and Dulles campus figures and whose shapes align to the official map context.
Fairfax and Loudoun parcel/land-use inventories are useful corroboration, but they materially undercount the full Dulles property and therefore are not sufficient as the primary build geometry.

cases.recommended_build_method: Do not build a production Port Authority police footprint from the currently public geometry sources. Keep the already-accepted broad overlap handling until a dedicated facility-by-facility geometry project is funded.
recommended_build_path: Use official documents such as the 2025 Budget Book https://www.panynj.gov/content/dam/corporate/budgets-pdfs/2025-Budget-Book.pdf, the police-services RFP https://www.panynj.gov/content/dam/port-authority/pdfs/goods-and-services-pdfs/RFPQDOC_6000000799.pdf, and the official statement https://www.panynj.gov/content/dam/corporate/consolidated-bonds-%26-notes-pdfs/port-authority-OS-series-251.pdf only to define system scope.

Do not rely on the public PANYNJ Facility layer https://geoapps.gis.panynj.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Hosted/Facility/FeatureServer/0 for production geometry. It is named Facility Old and exposes only department and facility codes, not facility names or boundary semantics.

Future geometry work will need separate build programs for airports, PATH, bridges and tunnels, bus terminal, World Trade Center, and marine-terminal assets, with facility-specific parcel or right-of-way methods.

sources.title: PANYNJ Hosted Facility layer
sources.format: ArcGIS REST polygon layer with JSON and geoJSON query support

source_hierarchy.reason: The layer is underdocumented, named Facility Old, has only four fields, uses opaque codes such as TB&T LT and RE BIP, includes duplicates, and does not prove that the polygons are property boundaries or police-jurisdiction extents.
These documents establish which facilities belong to the Port Authority system, but they do not provide property-accurate geometry.

A systemwide OSM fallback is not defensible here because airports, PATH, bridges, tunnels, ports, and the World Trade Center all require different official validation methods and the public official geometry package is incomplete.

validation_notes: This remains a later geometry project for a precise reason, not because the agency scope is unclear. Scope is clear; buildable public facility geometry is not.
The public Facility layer is evidence that PANYNJ maintains internal GIS, but the publicly exposed version is not documented well enough to convert into production overlap weights.
